E-scooter legislation, including licensing, insurance, helmets, age limits and road-use rules, falls under the Department for Transport's responsibility for road traffic and vehicle regulation.
The State Pension, including its eligibility age, rate and payment to expatriates, is the responsibility of the Department for Work and Pensions.
The Cabinet Office is responsible for constitutional issues such as general elections and the dissolution of Parliament.
The petition concerns NHS funding, staff training and facilities in psychiatric hospitals, which fall under the Department of Health and Social Care.
The petition concerns UK foreign policy and delivery of humanitarian aid to Gaza, including relations with Israel and the UN, which falls under the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.
Imposing sanctions on another state in response to its foreign conduct is a foreign policy matter led by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.
Traffic signs and parking signage regulations (Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions) are set by the Department for Transport.

The petition concerns UK foreign policy toward Israel and Gaza, including seeking a ceasefire and the arms export licensing decisions that the Foreign Secretary makes on International Humanitarian Law grounds.
Starting diplomatic talks with Canada, Australia and New Zealand on a union is a matter of foreign relations, which the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office handles.
Council tax policy and local government finance in England are the responsibility of the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government.
The petition asks for legislation requiring schools to hold spare auto-injectors, train staff and adopt allergy policies, which falls under the Department for Education's responsibility for schools.
Cancer screening programmes and NHS funding for investigating symptoms fall under the Department of Health and Social Care.
The petition concerns the statutory National Curriculum and teaching approaches in Key Stage 1 schools in England, which fall under the Department for Education.
The petition concerns police data collection and recording on child sexual offenders and grooming gangs, which is the Home Office's responsibility for policing and crime.
DEFRA is responsible for wildlife protection policy and the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, including the species listed on its schedules.

Employment law and labour market regulation, including pay transparency in job adverts, fall under the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (which now covers the former Department for Business and Trade's employment rights remit).
The petition asks for a new criminal offence, and criminal law and sentencing policy fall under the Ministry of Justice, though the Home Office also has related responsibilities.
The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero is responsible for North Sea oil and gas licensing policy through the North Sea Transition Authority and for energy and net zero policy.
The petition asks for funded routine Type 1 Diabetes screening for infants and children in NHS care, which is a health policy and funding matter for the Department of Health and Social Care.
The Ministry of Justice is responsible for prisons and the employment terms of Prison Officers, including their pension and retirement arrangements.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, including BN(O) visa routes and indefinite leave to remain requirements.
Relations with the EU, including any decision to rejoin, are handled by the Cabinet Office's Europe/EU relations ministerial portfolio rather than the FCDO's day-to-day foreign policy.
The petition asks for changes to the school curriculum (PSHE/Biology), which is the responsibility of the Department for Education.
The petition targets the DWP's Pathways to Work Green Paper and proposed disability benefit reforms, which fall under the Department for Work and Pensions.
School attendance rules and fines for term-time absence, including for children with special educational needs, are the responsibility of the Department for Education.
The petition concerns sentencing and the use of prison for offences, which is the responsibility of the Ministry of Justice.
The petition is about preventing wildlife and pets from being ensnared in sports netting, which falls under DEFRA's responsibility for animal welfare and wildlife protection.
The petition concerns transferring surplus British Army Warrior armoured vehicles to Ukraine, which is a matter of military equipment and defence support handled by the Ministry of Defence.
Pet travel rules and animal health certification are the responsibility of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, which would lead any arrangement on the EU pet passport scheme.
Chalk stream recovery, river conservation, water abstraction and pollution regulation fall under the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
NHS prescription charge exemptions for medical conditions are set by the Department of Health and Social Care.
The petition asks the Department for Education to change school attendance coding guidance so flexischooling is recorded distinctly and does not count against attendance data.
Banning full-face coverings in public is chiefly a public order, policing and security matter, which falls under the Home Office.
The petition concerns the UK-EU relationship, which the Cabinet Office leads, and it asks for a referendum, a constitutional matter, rather than a defence spending or operational decision.
The Home Office is responsible for asylum policy, including accommodation and financial support for asylum seekers under the asylum support system.
The petition concerns requirements for schools and colleges on safety equipment and staff training, which falls under the Department for Education's responsibilities.
DEFRA is responsible for animal welfare policy and the Animal Welfare Act 2006, including breeder licensing, dog ownership rules and cruelty penalties.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, including Indefinite Leave to Remain rules for Skilled Worker visa holders.
Income tax rules, thresholds and exemptions, including the tax treatment of the state pension, are the responsibility of HM Treasury (with HMRC).

The petition concerns onshore wind planning regulations and renewable energy development policy, which fall under the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, though DEFRA has an interest in peatland protection.
The Cabinet Office leads on UK-EU relations and the post-Brexit relationship, so it would respond on whether to commission an inquiry into the impact of leaving the EU.
The petition concerns NHS recruitment and employment of newly qualified nurses into Band 5 roles, which falls under the Department of Health and Social Care's responsibility for NHS workforce policy.
DEFRA is responsible for animal welfare policy and legislation, including licensing and inspection of animal rescue and rehoming activities.
The petition concerns teacher and school staff training requirements and inclusion of neurodivergent pupils in education, which is the responsibility of the Department for Education.
DEFRA is responsible for waste policy and landfill regulation, including the Environment Agency, which licenses and enforces rules on landfill emissions and odours.
DEFRA is responsible for food policy, agriculture, and the public-funded meat and dairy promotion campaigns (e.g. via the AHDB), as well as the environmental and climate aspects of farming.
Ambulance staff are NHS employees, and the NHS Pension Scheme and its retirement ages are the responsibility of the Department of Health and Social Care, working with HM Treasury.
Wildlife protection, game species and animal welfare policy, including close seasons for hares, fall under the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
MHCLG is responsible for the Greater London Authority, devolution and local government, including the rules for Mayor of London elections and who is eligible to vote in them.
The DVSA, which runs driving test booking and the theory test certificate, is an executive agency of the Department for Transport.
The petition calls for changes to Home Office licensing and scheduling of cannabis under the Misuse of Drugs Act, which is a Home Office responsibility.
The petition concerns legal rights to assessment and support for children with SEND under the Children and Families Act 2014, which is education policy led by the Department for Education.
Housing, leasehold and landlord service charge regulation fall under the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government.
The petition asks for a legal right to NHS gender transition treatment, including hormones and surgery, which is a matter of NHS healthcare policy under the Department of Health and Social Care.
Waste policy and environmental permitting for incinerators in England fall under the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
The Home Office is responsible for nationality and British citizenship policy, including the 'good character requirement' guidance and its treatment of refugees.
The petition concerns standards of conduct for MPs and political integrity, plus a new independent fact-check body, which falls under the Cabinet Office's remit for constitutional affairs and ethics.
The Department for Work and Pensions is responsible for the state pension and the rates at which pensioner benefits are paid.
Animal welfare law, including the Animal Welfare Act 2006 and its penalties and disqualification orders, is the responsibility of DEFRA.
The petition is about disability benefits and support for people unable to work, which the Department for Work and Pensions is responsible for.
The petition concerns the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill and home education policy, which is the responsibility of the Department for Education.
The Home Office is responsible for nationality law, citizenship and immigration policy, including the BN(O) visa route and British nationality status.
DCMS is responsible for the UK's UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Convention work and for heritage, culture and the pub and hospitality sector.
DCMS is responsible for the listed events regime that designates Category A sporting events for free-to-air broadcasting.
The Home Office is responsible for asylum accommodation, immigration policy and the deportation of people with no right to remain in the UK.
Statutory maternity and paternity pay rates are set by the Department for Work and Pensions, which handles statutory payments and the benefits system.
The petition concerns Northern Ireland Troubles legacy legislation and prosecutions, which the Northern Ireland Office leads.
Royal Mail and postal services policy, including the Universal Service Obligation and Postal Services Act legislation, falls under the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.
The Tobacco and Vapes Bill and the regulation of vape flavours for public health are led by the Department of Health and Social Care.
The Cabinet Office is responsible for UK constitutional policy, including general election arrangements and the Fixed-term Parliaments/Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act.
The petition concerns NHS Parkinson's diagnosis, specialist care, and health research funding, which fall under the Department of Health and Social Care.

The petition seeks to ban geo-engineering interventions in the environment, which falls mainly under environmental policy and regulation, though Greenhouse Gas Removal also touches on net zero policy.
The petition seeks new criminal offences and police powers over carrying and selling catapults, which is a Home Office responsibility covering policing, crime and offensive weapons.
The petition asks for more funding for FND education, awareness and training for health professionals, which falls under health policy and the NHS.
The petition asks for funding for healthcare professional training and specialist NHS facilities for people with PoTS, which falls under the Department of Health and Social Care.
The Home Office is responsible for policing, child sexual exploitation policy and commissioning statutory public inquiries into grooming gangs.
Solar energy policy and large-scale solar scheme approvals (Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects) fall under the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.
Knife crime, policing powers such as stop and search, and violence reduction units fall under the Home Office, which is also responsible for crime policy in England and Wales.
Policy on the Gender Recognition Act and equality law is led by the Equality Hub, within the Cabinet Office, under the Minister for Women and Equalities.
The petition concerns restrictions on prescribing puberty blockers in the NHS and private healthcare, which is health policy under the Department of Health and Social Care.
The petition asks for changes to the national curriculum for schools in England, which the Department for Education is responsible for.
The Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme concerns sentencing and criminal justice procedure, which the Ministry of Justice is responsible for (though the Attorney General's Office administers it).
The petition concerns visa extensions and indefinite leave to remain for Ukrainians in the UK, which are immigration matters handled by the Home Office.
Carer's Allowance is a social security benefit administered and set by the Department for Work and Pensions.
The Department for Education is responsible for education policy, including GCSE exam funding and support for home-educated children.
The Cabinet Office handles constitutional matters and referendums, and also leads on UK-EU relations.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, including the rules on Indefinite Leave to Remain and the qualifying period for settlement.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, including the Electronic Travel Authorisation scheme and entry requirements for BN(O) passport holders.
The Gender Recognition Act 2004 and the Gender Recognition Panel fall under the Ministry of Justice.
Political donations and party finance rules are now handled by MHCLG, which took over electoral and democracy policy, including the Elections Act and Electoral Commission oversight.
The petition concerns how the DWP runs Personal Independence Payment assessments and reassessments, which is the responsibility of the Department for Work and Pensions.

The petition asks for a day-one financial grant for parents of seriously ill children before they qualify for benefits such as Disability Living Allowance, which falls under the Department for Work and Pensions.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, including visas and settlement routes such as those for Ukrainians in the UK.

The Dangerous Dogs Act is a Home Office matter, but the petition is mainly about dog control and animal welfare, including a leash law around horses, which DEFRA covers; the Home Office is the alternative.
Income tax thresholds and allowances are set by HM Treasury as part of fiscal policy and Budget decisions.
Bus lane access rules for motorcycles are a transport policy matter, and the consultation was run by the Department for Transport.
The petition concerns NHS funding and access to CAR T cell therapy as a cancer treatment, which falls under health policy.
Farm animal welfare, including bans on cages and crates for farmed animals, is the responsibility of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
The Chagos Islands sovereignty agreement with Mauritius is a foreign policy and overseas territories matter handled by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.
The petition calls for a national referendum, which falls under Cabinet Office responsibility for constitutional affairs and referendum legislation.
Food labelling and livestock feed additives fall under the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, which oversees agriculture, food standards policy and farm emissions.
The English National Concessionary Travel Scheme for free bus travel is run by the Department for Transport.
The Climate Change Act 2008 and Net Zero targets are the responsibility of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.
The petition concerns prison sentencing and early release rules for offenders, which fall under the Ministry of Justice.
Consumer protection law, including the Consumer Rights Act and digital content rules, is the responsibility of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.
The petition concerns NHS constitution changes on how transgender patients are accommodated in hospital wards, which is a matter for the Department of Health and Social Care.
The petition concerns the State Pension and means-tested pensioner benefits such as Pension Credit, which are the responsibility of the Department for Work and Pensions.
The petition asks to reverse funding cuts to the Sea, Army and RAF Cadet Forces and Combined Cadet Forces, which the Ministry of Defence funds and oversees.
Non-crime hate incidents are recorded by police under College of Policing guidance, and policing policy and crime recording fall under the Home Office.
The Department for Work and Pensions is responsible for the State Pension, including its age of entitlement and the level at which it is set.
Driven grouse shooting regulation involves moorland management, wildlife protection, muirburn and upland environment policy, which fall under the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
The petition concerns NHS gender services for children and the Cass review, which was commissioned by NHS England and falls under health policy.
The Ministry of Justice is responsible for human rights law, including the Human Rights Act and UK adherence to the ECHR.
DCMS is responsible for the TV licence fee and BBC funding, including concessions for over-75s, while Pension Credit eligibility is only a secondary aspect of the petition.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, including visa routes and indefinite leave to remain requirements.
Badger culling and bovine TB control policy is the responsibility of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
DEFRA is responsible for animal welfare policy and the regulation of animal slaughter in the UK.
Income tax thresholds such as the Personal Allowance are set by HM Treasury, which is responsible for tax policy.
The petition concerns school attendance rules and fines for term-time leave, which are the responsibility of the Department for Education.
HM Treasury is responsible for financial services policy, including legislation on access to cash and the banking sector's cash infrastructure.
The TV licence fee and BBC funding and governance are the responsibility of the Department for Culture, Media and Sport.
Abortion policy and the Abortion Act 1967 fall under the Department of Health and Social Care, which usually responds to petitions on abortion law.
The petition asks for a government public information campaign on climate science and the actions needed to reach net zero, which falls under the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.
The petition concerns compensation for women affected by State Pension age increases and DWP maladministration in communicating them, which falls under the Department for Work and Pensions.
Responsibility for elections policy and electoral system reform now sits with the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government.
Regulation of fireworks sales and consumer use falls under the business department's product safety remit, via the Office for Product Safety and Standards.
Calling a general election and the dissolution of Parliament are constitutional matters handled by the Cabinet Office.
The petition concerns constitutional matters, including the law on political parties' manifestos and the triggering of general elections, which are Cabinet Office responsibilities.
The Home Office is responsible for immigration policy, border control, and both legal and illegal migration.
Employer National Insurance rates and exemptions are tax policy set by HM Treasury, even though the petition concerns the social care sector.
The petition concerns sponsored work visa rules and sponsor licensing for foreign care workers, which UK Visas and Immigration under the Home Office is responsible for.
Inheritance tax policy, including agricultural property relief, is set by HM Treasury, which is responsible for tax policy.
The Winter Fuel Payment is a social security benefit for pensioners that the Department for Work and Pensions administers and sets policy for.
The Cabinet Office is responsible for the UK's relationship with the EU, including EU relations and any decision on rejoining, so it would answer this petition.
The petition seeks to restrict fossil fuel promotion as a way to phase out fossil fuels and tackle climate change, which falls under the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero's remit.
VAT on school fees is a tax policy set by HM Treasury, which is responsible for VAT legislation, although business rates relief is a local government matter.
